metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Acids, Bases, Salts — Definition of a Normal Salt
metadata.note: 2m: define normal salt. Cloze: [[1]](0.5m) the replaceable [[2]](0.5m) of [[3]](0.5m) have been replaced by [[4]](0.5m). Key discriminator: ALL replaceable H⁺ — 'partial' is wrong (that describes an acid salt). 'OH⁻' and 'base' are distractors.

question.name: CSEC Chem Jan 2023 Q1a(i) — Define Normal Salt
question.text:
Define the term 'normal salt' by completing the statement below:

A normal salt is formed when [[1]] the replaceable [[2]] of [[3]] have been replaced by [[4]].
question.general_feedback:
Normal salt definition:

A normal salt is formed when ALL the replaceable hydrogen atoms (H⁺ ions) of an acid have been replaced by a metal (or ammonium ion).

Examples: NaCl (sodium chloride), Na₂SO₄ (sodium sulphate), CaCO₃ (calcium carbonate)

Contrast: An acid salt is formed when only SOME of the replaceable hydrogen atoms are replaced — e.g., NaHSO₄ (sodium hydrogensulphate) or NaHCO₃ (sodium hydrogencarbonate).

Note: The key word is ALL — this distinguishes a normal salt from an acid salt.

ddwtos.cloze_html: A normal salt is formed when [[1]] the replaceable [[2]] of [[3]] have been replaced by [[4]].

groups.label: Normal salt — ___ hydrogen atoms replaced
groups.diagnostic_hint: In a normal salt ALL acidic hydrogen atoms of the parent acid are replaced by metal ions (or ammonium). If only SOME are replaced it is an acid salt, not a normal salt.

groups.label: Normal salt — replaces ___ from the acid
groups.diagnostic_hint: The particles replaced are the hydrogen atoms (H⁺ ions) from the acid. For example, in HCl both H and Cl make HCl, but in NaCl the Na has replaced the H⁺.

groups.label: Normal salt — formed from ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: A salt is formed when a metal (or ammonium) replaces the hydrogen of an acid. The source is always an acid — a base/alkali provides the metal ion, but the salt itself comes from the acid framework.

groups.label: Normal salt — the replacing ion is ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: The hydrogen is replaced by a metal ion (e.g. Na⁺, Ca²⁺) or ammonium ion (NH₄⁺). Non-metals and OH⁻ ions do not replace H⁺ to form a normal salt.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 16 tokens for 4 slots. Slot 1 (all/some/partial/none): 'some' is the key distractor — choosing 'some' describes an ACID salt (e.g. NaHSO₄), not a normal salt. 'Partial' and 'none' are also wrong. Slot 2 (hydrogen atoms or H⁺ ions): both accepted as equivalent. 'OH⁻ ions' is wrong — OH⁻ comes from bases, not acids. Slot 3 (an acid / the acid): both accepted. 'A base' and 'an alkali' are wrong — the definition concerns the acid's H⁺. Slot 4 (a metal / a metal or ammonium): both accepted. 'Non-metal' and 'OH⁻ ions' are wrong replacements.
